# Constraint2D

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- **Not creatable**: `Instance.new` refuses it
- **Abstract**: it exists to be inherited from

The base of a joint between two `Part2D`s (ADR 0102): the 2D solver holds them together, and a rope bridge, a door on a hinge or a swinging lamp is what comes of it.

**Two parts and a point on each**, not two attachments: a 2D joint is a point, and each part's is in that part's own metres from its middle. A joint that cannot hold -- a part that is missing or is not in the world, or two anchored parts -- holds nothing and is not an error.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Anchor0` | `Vector2` | — | read/write | Where the joint is on `Part0`, in metres from its middle, in its own frame, so it turns with the part. |
| `Anchor1` | `Vector2` | — | read/write | Where the joint is on `Part1`, the same way. |
| `CollideConnected` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the two parts still collide with each other. False is what a chain of links or a limb wants, where the parts overlap at the joint by construction. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the joint holds. A disabled joint stays in the world holding nothing. |
| `Part0` | `Part2D?` | — | read/write | One of the two parts it holds. |
| `Part1` | `Part2D?` | — | read/write | The other. |
